question: Which moderate leader, often referred to as the 'Grand Old Man of India,' became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons and helped shape the early nationalist movement? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: Rash Behari Ghosh
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Dadabhai Naoroji
Pherozeshah Mehta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He became the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 from Finsbury Central. As a moderate leader, he played a crucial role in the early years of the Indian National Congress and served as its president three times. His famous 'Drain of Wealth' theory exposed the economic exploitation of India under British rule. He advocated for Swaraj and helped shape the early nationalist movement. He also wrote the influential book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

question_hi: कौन से उदारवादी नेता, जिन्हें अक्सर 'भारत का ग्रैंड ओल्ड मैन' कहा जाता है, ब्रिटिश हाउस ऑफ कॉमन्स के लिए चुने गए पहले भारतीय बने और जिन्होंने प्रारंभिक राष्ट्रवादी आंदोलन को आकार देने में मदद की? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (21/06/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: Which of the following reformers was NOT associated with British India?  (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (19/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Aryabhatta
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Swami Vivekananda
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aryabhatta

Explanation:
Aryabhatta was an ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer, who lived around the 5th century CE, long before the British India period. Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Swami Vivekananda were social-religious reformers and nationalist leaders during the 19th and 20th centuries under British rule. Raja Ram Mohan Roy is known as the 'Father of Indian Renaissance' and played a key role in the abolition of Sati. Bal Gangadhar Tilak was a prominent freedom fighter, popularly called 'Lokmanya'. Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission. Therefore, Aryabhatta was not associated with British India.

question: The exile of the ruler of which kingdom was termed as "The life has gone out of the body"? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 1)
options: Punjab
Maratha lands
Bengal
Awadh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Awadh

Explanation:
The exile of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh in 1856 was termed by contemporary newspapers as "The life has gone out of the body". He was the last ruler of Awadh. Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh on the pretext of misgovernance under the Doctrine of Lapse. Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta (Kolkata). He was a patron of arts and music. His exile caused widespread discontent among the people of Awadh, which later became one of the causes of the Revolt of 1857. The annexation of Awadh was a major event in British colonial history.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
अवध के शासक वाजिद अली शाह को अंग्रेजों ने 1856 में निर्वासित कर दिया था। उनके निर्वासन को तत्कालीन समाचारपत्रों ने "शरीर से प्राण निकल गया" कहा था। वाजिद अली शाह अवध के अंतिम नवाब थे। उन पर कुशासन का आरोप लगाकर लॉर्ड डलहौजी ने राज्य को ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य में मिला लिया। यह घटना अवध के विलय के रूप में जानी जाती है। वाजिद अली शाह को कलकत्ता (कोलकाता) भेज दिया गया। वे कला और संगीत के संरक्षक थे। उनके निर्वासन से अवध की जनता में असंतोष फैल गया, जो 1857 के विद्रोह का एक कारण बना।

question: Which session of the congress gave a call to the attainment of 'Swaraj'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (29/12/2020) Shift 1)
options: 1909
1906
1904
1902
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1906

Explanation:
The 1906 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, gave the first call for the attainment of 'Swaraj' (self-rule). In his presidential address, Naoroji declared that India needed self-government. This session marked a significant shift in the Congress from moderate to militant nationalism. It was a turning point in the Indian freedom movement. Following this, the Congress split at the 1907 Surat session. The demand for Swaraj became a central theme in the struggle for independence. Dadabhai Naoroji, known as the Grand Old Man of India, played a key role in articulating the political aspirations of Indians.

question: Who devised the policy of Doctrine of Lapse? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (30/12/2020) Shift 2)
options: Lord Dalhousie
General Dyer
Lord Hastings
Lord Clive
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lord Dalhousie

Explanation:
The policy of Doctrine of Lapse was devised by Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856). According to this policy, if a ruler of a princely state had no natural heir, the state would be annexed by the British Empire. Adopted sons were not recognized as legitimate successors. Using this policy, the British annexed states like Satara (1848), Nagpur (1853), Jhansi (1854), and Awadh (1856). This policy significantly contributed to the causes of the Revolt of 1857.

☛ Which state was first annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse? → Satara (1848)
☛ Which queen was affected by the Doctrine of Lapse? → Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi)
☛ What was the tenure of Lord Dalhousie as Governor-General? → 1848-1856
☛ What was the impact of the Doctrine of Lapse on the 1857 Revolt? → It was a major cause of the revolt

Explanation:
व्यपगत के सिद्धांत की नीति लॉर्ड डलहौजी (1848-1856) द्वारा प्रतिपादित की गई थी। इस नीति के अनुसार, यदि किसी रियासत के शासक का कोई प्राकृतिक पुत्र नहीं था, तो वह रियासत ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य में विलीन हो जाती थी। गोद लिए पुत्रों को उत्तराधिकार का अधिकार नहीं दिया जाता था। इस नीति का उपयोग करके अंग्रेजों ने सतारा (1848), नागपुर (1853), झाँसी (1854) और अवध (1856) जैसी रियासतों को हड़प लिया। इस नीति ने 1857 के विद्रोह के कारणों में से एक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।

question: The first national flag of India is said to have hoisted at _______ in 1906. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/01/2021) Shift 1)
options: Patna
Kolkata
New Delhi
Ahmedabad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kolkata

Explanation:
The first national flag of India was hoisted on 7 August 1906 at Parsi Bagan Chowk (now Baratiya Bhavan Square) in Kolkata. The flag had three colors: green, yellow, and red, with eight lotus flowers, a crescent moon, and a sun. It was also known as the Bharat Swabhiman Flag. The flag was unfurled by Shachindra Prasad Bose and Sukhalal Yadav. This event took place during the Swadeshi movement, symbolizing the boycott of British goods. Later, in 1917, Madam Bhikaji Rustom Cama unfurled another version of the Indian flag.

question: Which policy of the British greatly affected the tribal landholding patterns and led to widespread discontent among the tribes, thereby fueling rebellions (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (24/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Ryotwari System
Forest laws and land settlements
Permanent Settlement
Doctrine of Lapse
solution:

Explanation:
The British introduced forest laws and land settlements that severely disrupted the traditional landholding patterns of tribal communities. These laws restricted the tribes' access to forest resources, which were essential for their livelihood and culture. Additionally, land settlements transferred ownership to non-tribal zamindars, leading to alienation and displacement of tribals. This caused widespread discontent and sparked numerous rebellions, such as the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) and the Birsa Munda Rebellion (1899-1900). The forest laws and land settlements thus played a major role in fueling tribal uprisings.

question: Who among the following was the first Indian member of The British Parliament? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (08/04/2021) Shift 2)

question: In which year did Bakshi Jagabandhu lead the Paika Rebellion to protest against the British land revenue policy? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (05/06/2025) Shift 1)

question: Who was the first Portuguese Governor to implement the "Blue Water Policy" in India? (RRB NTPC GRADUATE CBT 1 (25/03/2026) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:
Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870 on financial decentralization laid the foundation for the development of local self-government institutions in India. Hobhouse chaired the Royal Commission on Decentralization (1907), which recommended devolution of powers to provinces. Under the Government of India Act of 1919, local self-government was made a transferred subject, not a reserved subject.
